samples.summary: clearImageSelectionForMutation() (and imageKeyHandler's catch-all) drop the image selection without aborting an in-flight resize drag, so a mutation during a drag can commit the drag's size onto a different image
samples.evidence: `clearImageSelectionForMutation` (editor.ts:1290-1294) sets `selectedImage = null; render();` but never calls `abortImageResizeDrag()`. Same at editor.ts:2449 (imageKeyHandler catch-all) and editor.ts:2679 (click-elsewhere branch). `abortImageResizeDrag`'s own doc comment (editor.ts:2576-2580) states the invariant: "every path that clears the image selection because the offsets moved under it has to drop the drag too, or the next `mouseup` commits the drag's size onto whatever inline now sits at that coordinate." undoFn/redoFn/resetAfterDocumentReplace honour it; the shared helper does not. Reachable: hold a resize handle, press ⌘V (keydown hits the catch-all, paste hits `imageSelectionClearer`) — the drag stays armed and `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (editor.ts:2549) then applies the size to whatever image now sits at the captured (blockId, offset). The `!current` guard only stops it when the slot no longer holds an image; a different image at that offset is silently resized.

samples.summary: handleCopy with a text selection and a null clipboardData now returns without preventDefault, letting the native copy of the empty hidden textarea wipe the system clipboard — the exact failure the new guard's comment says it prevents
samples.evidence: The guard was hoisted above the selection check: `const clipboard = e.clipboardData; if (!clipboard) return;` (text-editor.ts:1205-1206). Previously the text path ran `e.preventDefault()` first and then used `e.clipboardData?.setData(...)`, so a null clipboardData left the system clipboard untouched. Now the handler returns uncancelled, so the browser performs its default copy against the hidden textarea (always empty — see text-editor.ts:805 `this.textarea.value = ''`), which can replace the user's clipboard with an empty string. The comment at 1201-1204 claims this ordering avoids exactly that outcome; for the text-selection path it introduces it.

samples.summary: An active IME composition bypasses imageKeyHandler entirely, so composed text can be inserted while an image selection stays live and stale
samples.evidence: `handleKeyDown` returns at text-editor.ts:852 (`if (this.composition.active || e.isComposing) return;`) before the `imageKeyHandler` hook at :865. The whole PR rests on the catch-all at editor.ts:2449 clearing `selectedImage` on any key that mutates text. A user composing (composition already active), who then clicks an image — `handleImageMouseDown` stops propagation so nothing flushes the composition — and continues typing will have the composed text committed at the caret while `selectedImage` still names the old (blockId, offset). The stale coordinate then names whichever inline slid into the slot; `imageSelectionProvider` only re-validates that *an* image is there, so a subsequent ⌘C/Delete can act on the wrong image.

samples.summary: getSelectedTableCells() was moved to getActiveLayout() but still resolves the table block with layout.blocks.find, so a cell-rectangle copy/cut in a nested table writes an empty rich payload (and cut still deletes)
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts:3761 `const lb = layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cr.blockId);` — `layout.blocks` only holds top-level blocks, so an inner table's id never resolves and the function returns null. `getSelectedBlocks()` was explicitly fixed for this case with `resolveNestedTableLayout` (text-editor.ts:3808) but its sibling was not, even though the diff's comment at 3753-3755 treats the two as the same fix. handleCopy/handleCut then fall through to getSelectedBlocks, whose start/end live in different cells, yielding `[]`; handleCut (text-editor.ts:1274-1279) still preventDefaults, writes `{"blocks":[]}` and calls deleteSelection(), so the styled cell content is deleted with only plain text on the clipboard.

samples.summary: Removing the read-only early return from handleImageMouseDown makes image clicks consume the event in read-only, so a viewer can no longer start a text drag-selection on an image
samples.evidence: `handleImageMouseDown` no longer starts with `if (readOnly) return;` (editor.ts:2609-2611) and the image-body branch calls `e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); e.stopImmediatePropagation();` (editor.ts:2659-2667). In read-only, `TextEditor.handleMouseDown` therefore never runs for an image press, so `isMouseDown`/selection anchor bookkeeping (text-editor.ts:1680+) is skipped: a viewer dragging a text selection that begins on an image now gets nothing instead of a selection. Only the link bookkeeping was re-armed (`recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse`); the drag-selection path was not.
